newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says northern Iraq operation goes on.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says northern Iraq operation goes on.

text.p: Turkey is continuing its six-week-old incursion into northern Iraq in pursuit of Kurdish rebels despite a partial troop pullout, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman, quoted by the Anatolian news agency, said some Turkish troops remained in northern Iraq in support of Iraqi Kurdish groups, the agency said. Troops, armoured vehicles and tanks began to return to Turkey last week.

More than 10,000 Turkish soldier poured across the border into northern Iraq from May 14 in an attempt to eliminate Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels from the region, which the guerrillas use as a base for raids into Turkey.
Turkish forces were supported by fighters of Iraq's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) who Turkey says invited its troops into the region. KDP spokesmen do not confirm this.
Much of the Arab world and some of Turkey's Western allies have condemned Ankara for its incursion into the Kurdish-held region, out of Baghdad's control since after the 1991 Gulf War.
Turkey says it has killed more than 2,600 PKK fighters in the operation for the loss of 99 of its own soldiers and members of village guard militia.
The entire campaign has been carried out under a strict news blackout, with correspondents barred from the region and communications blocked, making independent confirmation of events impossible.
However, Western diplomats say the reported PKK death toll is exaggerated.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict between the Turkish security forces and the PKK, fighting for Kurdish autonomy or independence.
